title: Detection of Large Dense-Core Vesicle Exocytosis Using Automated Image Processing
author: Makam, Ramadas, et al.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Obtain ethical clearance for human pancreatic islet work and follow BSL‑2 safety; prepare sterile CMRL‑1066 culture medium, imaging buffer and cell‑dissociation buffer; keep reagents at recommended storage conditions; calibrate the TIRF microscope and verify laser alignment; prepare adenovirus stocks for granule markers (NPY‑Venus or NPY‑mCherry) and Lipofectamine 2000; install and verify the Lagrangian particle‑tracking algorithm on the imaging workstation; dispose of all biohazardous waste according to institutional policy.

steps.title: Isolate and culture human pancreatic islets
steps.instruction: Obtain human pancreatic islets from cadaveric donors with approved consent; culture them in CMRL‑1066 medium supplemented with 5.5 mM glucose, 10 % fetal calf serum, 2 mM L‑glutamine, 100 U mL⁻¹ penicillin and 100 U mL⁻¹ streptomycin; maintain cultures at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂ for approximately two weeks, keeping sterility throughout.

steps.title: Disperse islets into single cells
steps.instruction: Wash islets twice with Ca²⁺‑free cell‑dissociation buffer; treat with 1× trypsin (0.05 %) and incubate at 37 °C for 5–10 min with gentle agitation; add serum‑containing medium to stop the reaction; transfer cells to a Corning conical tube and centrifuge at 300 × g to pellet; resuspend the pellet in fresh serum‑containing medium.

steps.title: Plate cells and perform transfection
steps.instruction: Rinse 22 mm glass coverslips with 70 % ethanol and air‑dry; place coverslips in a six‑well plate; add 0.01 % w/v Poly‑L‑Lysine in PBS (~500 µL per well) to fully cover each coverslip and incubate 20 min at 25 °C; rinse 2–3 times with PBS and air‑dry in a sterile laminar flow hood; seed cells at 50 000–100 000 cells per coverslip and incubate 12–16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; transfect by adding 100 µL OptiMEM containing 0.5 µg plasmid DNA (NPY‑GFP or NPY‑mCherry) and 0.5 µL Lipofectamine 2000, incubate 5–6 h, then replace with complete serum‑containing medium; optionally transfect with eGFP‑tagged constructs using the same reagent; image cells 24–36 h after transfection.

steps.title: Immobilize fluorescent beads on coverslip
steps.instruction: Dilute 100 nm TetraSpeck beads 1:100 in 1× PBS; dispense 10 µL of the diluted suspension onto a 22‑mm coverslip; let beads settle for 10 min at 25 °C; gently wash 2–3 times with 1× PBS to remove unbound beads; image the beads using TIRF microscopy if desired.

steps.title: Generate artificial validation images
steps.instruction: Create circular objects using (x±x₁)²+(y+y₁)² ≤ r², varying the radius r to obtain different vesicle areas (distinct, tangent, intersecting); generate several noisy versions (Gaussian, Poisson) and normalize each image to the range [0, 1]; compose the final image as Final = w₁·Noise₁ + w₂·Noise₂ + (1‑(w₁+w₂))·Raw, adjusting radius and noise weights to mimic TIRF images.

steps.title: Manual particle counting (by eye)
steps.instruction: Open each image in Metamorph, count particles manually, record the total number of particles per image, compute the average across images, and calculate the standard error of the mean (SEM) for each experimental condition.

steps.title: Find Maxima detection in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Load the image onto Fiji (ImageJ); select the appropriate macros and the built‑in ‘Find Maxima’ plugin; draw a region of interest (ROI) around the cell; run the plugin to detect particles; record the total particle count, average values across images, and compute the SEM for each condition.

steps.title: Run automated Lagrangian tracking algorithm
steps.instruction: Load acquired images into the Lagrangian particle‑tracking algorithm; detect punctate structures (vesicles) and quantify intensity changes over time; compare the algorithm’s results with those obtained by the ImageJ Find Maxima method and manual counting for validation.
